text: Five thousand rupees a month can become fifty lakh. So why does your SIP feel useless?
Say you invest five thousand rupees a month.
After five years, you've put in three lakh. It's worth about four lakh. Feels slow.
After ten years: six lakh in. About eleven and a half lakh.
After twenty years: twelve lakh in. About fifty lakh.
Same SIP. Same amount. The growth just shows up late.
That's compounding. Your returns start earning their own returns.
And most people quit in year three, right before the curve bends.
This assumes twelve percent a year. Real returns go up and down, and nothing is guaranteed.
So don't judge your SIP by year one. Judge it by year fifteen.
